title: Graded DCA run classification block
description: The run_classification object embedded in every run_state artifact. It is the single authoritative signal that distinguishes a scheduled live run of the repaired live task 10ce362c (which supersedes the deleted ce16ba6b) from an ad-hoc manual run so downstream slippage/watchdog/weekly reporting never confuses the two. Also accepts the 10:30/12:30 seven-slot-roster identities run_dca.run_slot() stamps via scripts.run_classification.build_scheduled_classification's stream override (see the morning/midday anyOf branches below) -- those slots additionally have their OWN dedicated, richer schemas (morning_run_classification.schema.json, midday_run_classification.schema.json) written for MorningDCAExecutor/MiddayDCAExecutor's own native artifact shape (run_type='morning_dca_live', run_id='morning_live_YYYYMMDD_1030ET', etc); the roster deliberately does NOT produce that shape, since it routes 10:30/12:30 through this generic afternoon-shaped pipeline instead of those executors' own live mode (Codex review discussion_r3694539239, 'Keep roster classifications valid under their stream schemas' -- confirmed as an accepted scope limit, not a live gap: no code outside those executors and their own tests reads either dedicated schema or MorningDCAExecutor's/MiddayDCAExecutor's own latest_morning_run.json/latest_midday_run.json pointer files, and both executors' own live-mode callers have already been superseded by this roster). This generic schema only guarantees the identity fields it has always covered stay internally coherent. Contains no secrets.

run_origin.description: Authoritative origin of the run. 'scheduled' is reserved for the live cron task 10ce362c firing inside its window; 'manual_user_cap_override' is a manual run where the user explicitly overrode the daily/weekly cap (e.g. the Aug 18 2026 incident -- see docs/schedule_manifest.md and scripts.run_classification.RUN_ORIGIN_MANUAL_USER_CAP_OVERRIDE/is_top_up_context_state); everything else is 'manual'.

manual_run.description: true for manual runs, false for scheduled runs. Must agree with run_origin: manual_run === (run_origin == 'manual').

run_type.description: Free-form run type label. Scheduled live runs use 'scheduled_live_test'. Manual final-buy overrides (the final-buy decision requested manually, e.g. the 2026-07-13 incident) use 'final_manual_buy_override' and MUST carry run_origin='manual', manual_run=true, valid_afternoon_scheduled_evidence=false, and same_day_top_up_context_only=true.

valid_afternoon_scheduled_evidence.description: Whether this run counts as valid scheduled-afternoon execution evidence. Omitted/true for scheduled runs; MUST be false for run_type='final_manual_buy_override' so downstream slippage/watchdog/reliability/cost-basis reporting never treats a manual final override as scheduled evidence.

same_day_top_up_context_only.description: True for run_type='final_manual_buy_override' to mark its fills as same-day top-up / manual-override context only. Such fills appear only in the 'Manual Final Buy Override / Same-Day Top-Up Context' report section and never affect scheduled-live metrics.

cron_id.description: Live scheduled task id. Canonical value is '10ce362c' (the repaired live task; the deleted ce16ba6b is superseded). Placeholder or ambiguous values such as 'ce16ba6b_replacement' are forbidden. Carried on both scheduled and manual runs so manual runs can be attributed to the task they emulate.

supersedes_cron_id.description: Prior task id this run's task replaced, for lineage/continuity. Must be exactly 'ce16ba6b' (or null/omitted). Placeholder or ambiguous values such as 'ce16ba6b_replacement' are forbidden. This schema validates consumer acceptance/continuity: a scheduled run is accepted as valid evidence when cron_id='10ce362c' OR supersedes_cron_id='ce16ba6b' (see the anyOf below). The stricter writer contract, that every newly written scheduled 3:30 PM ET run_state carries BOTH cron_id='10ce362c' AND supersedes_cron_id='ce16ba6b', is enforced by the writer (scripts/run_classification.py) and documented in docs/run_classification.md, not by this schema.

scheduled_for_et.description: Nominal ET fire time of the scheduled task, HH:MM. '15:30' for scheduled runs since the 2026-07-27 retime of 10ce362c; '15:20' is accepted only for legacy runs that fired before that retime. '10:30'/'12:30' identify the seven-slot roster's morning/midday identities (stream='morning'/'midday'; see morning_run_classification.schema.json/midday_run_classification.schema.json for those streams' own dedicated, fuller contract). Null/omitted for manual runs.

scheduled_window_start_et.description: Inclusive start of the accepted scheduled window in ET, HH:MM. '15:20' for scheduled runs since 2026-11-14 (early-fire tolerance) and '15:25' for runs from the 2026-07-27 retime until then, both accepted; '15:15' is accepted only for legacy runs that fired before that retime. '10:25'/'12:25' for the morning/midday roster identities.

scheduled_window_end_et.description: Inclusive end of the accepted scheduled window in ET, HH:MM ('15:35', or '10:35'/'12:35' for the morning/midday roster identities).

run_id.description: Unique run id. Scheduled: 'scheduled_YYYYMMDD_1530ET' (legacy runs before the 2026-07-27 retime use 'scheduled_YYYYMMDD_1520ET'; the morning/midday roster identities use 'scheduled_YYYYMMDD_1030ET'/'scheduled_YYYYMMDD_1230ET'). Manual: a distinct id, e.g. 'manual_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSSZ', that never collides with the scheduled pattern.

triggered_at_utc.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the run was triggered.

state_schema_version.description: Version tag of the run-classification contract. 'run-classification-v1' is the original; 'run-classification-v2-preauthorized' is the stricter successor introduced 2026-07-10 for the pre-authorized direct-placement live task (no review_equity_order). Both are accepted as valid scheduled/manual evidence when the required scheduled identity fields (run_origin, manual_run, cron_id/supersedes_cron_id, scheduled_for_et, window, run_id) are correct; v2 is a stricter successor of v1, not a different contract. 'manual-override-v1' is the distinct contract for a run_origin='manual_user_cap_override' artifact (see the dedicated allOf branch below) -- never treated as scheduled/manual evidence itself.

allOf.description: Codex review discussion_r3653976747 ('Validate canonical and legacy identity fields as a unit'; discussion_r3694494920/r3694494922, 'Bind the window end to each slot identity'/'Validate the cron ID with the complete slot identity'): every identity-bearing field -- scheduled_for_et, scheduled_window_start_et, scheduled_window_end_et, run_id, stream, and cron lineage -- must agree within a SINGLE branch below, not be checked by independent anyOf lists. Independent lists let a record mix fields from different slots' identities (e.g. an afternoon time/run_id paired with the morning cron_id, or vice versa) and still validate, accepting a hybrid identity that names a slot which never exists. The legacy run_id pattern also enforces the retime date (Codex review r3654117261: 'Restrict legacy identities to pre-retime dates') so a stale or incorrectly written post-retime legacy artifact cannot conceal a missed canonical run; it mirrors CANONICAL_RETIME_DATE_YYYYMMDD in scripts/run_classification.py.

anyOf.description: Canonical afternoon (15:30 ET, since the 2026-07-27 retime). stream, when present, must be 'afternoon' or null: the morning/midday branches below require their own stream, but omitted this constraint here, an afternoon-shaped record could still claim stream='morning'/'midday' and validate, letting it be published through the wrong stream's pointer (Codex review: 'Require the afternoon stream in afternoon identity branches'). Not added to 'required': historical artifacts predating the stream field must stay valid. null is included alongside 'afternoon' (not just 'const': 'afternoon') because validate_classification() treats an EXPLICIT stream=null the same as absent legacy evidence, and update_latest_scheduled_run_pointer normalizes both to 'afternoon' when writing the pointer -- a bare 'const' rejected the present-but-null case those two already accept, splitting the schema and the standard-library path on the same artifact (Codex review: 'Accept null legacy streams in the schema').
Legacy afternoon (15:20 ET, strictly pre-retime dates). stream constraint and null-handling reasoning as the canonical branch above.

run_id.description: Legacy run_id, restricted to dates strictly before 2026-07-27 (the retime date).

anyOf.description: The seven-slot roster's 10:30 morning identity (run_dca.run_slot("1030ET") via scripts.run_classification.build_scheduled_classification's stream override). valid_afternoon_scheduled_evidence must be false: this is a morning-shaped record and must never be mistaken for afternoon evidence by a flag-based consumer that does not also cross-check stream (Codex review: 'Deny afternoon evidence in non-afternoon schema branches'). supersedes_cron_id must be null/absent, never the afternoon task's own 'ce16ba6b' lineage marker (Codex review: 'Reject afternoon supersession lineage on roster slots') -- constrained via 'const': null rather than 'not: required' so an explicit null (which the global property and validate_classification() both already treat as equivalent to absent) still validates; 'not: required' rejected the key whenever PRESENT, including null, so a serializer that retains optional fields as null failed this schema while validate_classification()/is_scheduled_state() accepted it (Codex review: 'Allow null supersession markers in roster branches').

The seven-slot roster's 12:30 midday identity (run_dca.run_slot("1230ET") via scripts.run_classification.build_scheduled_classification's stream override). valid_afternoon_scheduled_evidence and supersedes_cron_id constraints/reasoning as the morning branch above.

run_id.description: Excludes every official scheduled-slot run_id shape, including the seven-slot roster's 1030ET/1230ET identities, not just the original 1520/1530ET forms (Codex review: 'Exclude the new scheduled IDs from manual classifications').

allOf.description: A MANUAL USER CAP OVERRIDE (e.g. the Aug 18 2026 incident, config/scheduled_tasks.json's aug18_manual_cap_override and docs/schedule_manifest.md's incident bullet). Codex review, PR #656 follow-up: 'Define a schema for the new override origin' -- scripts.run_classification.RUN_ORIGIN_MANUAL_USER_CAP_OVERRIDE and is_top_up_context_state() already accept this run_origin at runtime, but the generic 'manual' allOf branch above never matches it (its if-condition is a bare const 'manual'), leaving this documented artifact shape with no schema coverage at all. Requires the same same_day_top_up_context_only=true / valid_scheduled_evidence=false markers every other manual-context artifact type (final_manual_buy_override, scheduled_recovery) already declares, plus the dedicated 'manual-override-v1' state_schema_version and 'manual_override' stream this shape uses instead of run_type.

run_id.description: Excludes every official scheduled-slot run_id shape, matching the plain 'manual' branch above.
